newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: G7 not meeting Chernobyl obligations, Ukraine says.
newsitem.headline: G7 not meeting Chernobyl obligations, Ukraine says.

text.p: The Group of Seven major industrial countries has not met its obligations to help Ukraine in the aftermath of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko said on Thursday.

He told a news conference Ukraine wanted to extricate about 180 tonnes of nuclear fuel from the concrete shell around the reactor damaged in 1986 and to build safe storage for it. It also wants to build two nuclear power reactors elsewhere to compensate for the loss of the remaining Chernobyl reactors, due to be closed down by 2000.

Udovenko said that when the G7 and the European Union asked for the Chernobyl power station to be closed down, Ukraine had said it would need technical assistance and financial help. The amount was to be negotiated by experts.

"Unfortunately, the G7 group does not fulfil its obligations to us in connection with the Chernobyl nuclear power station," he said. "We deal with all problems almost alone, without any substantive financial assistance. ... There is full political understanding by the G7 leaders ... of our problems but when it comes to technicalities it is always difficult to solve them."
Udovenko is expected to be elected president of the U.N. General Assembly when its session opens in September.

At its Denver summit last week, the G7 -- the United States, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan -- promised Ukraine $300 million to help rebuild the sarcophagus around the ruined Chernobyl nuclear reactor.
